source_text: Περὶ τῶν τριῶν εὐνουχισμῶν πνευματικῶς. Οἱ μὲν πρότεροι τοῦ γράμματος φίλοι τὸν τρίτον σωματικῶς τοῖς δυσὶν ἐξωμάλισαν· ἡμεῖς δὲ τὴν ἀκολουθίαν τῶν τριῶν εὐνουχισμῶν σῴζειν βουλόμενοι καὶ εὐδοκοῦντες τῇ τροπολογίᾳ τοῦ τρίτου, τοιαῦτα φήσομεν καὶ περὶ τῶν προτέρων δύο· εὐνοῦχοι τροπικῶς οἱ ἀργοὶ πρὸς ἀφροδίσια λεγοιντ’ ἄν. Διαφοραὶ δὲ τῶν πρὸς ταῦτα ἀργούντων τρεῖς· οἱ μὲν ἐκ κατασκευῆς τοιοῦτοι, περὶ ὧν· «Εἰσὶν εὐνοῦχοι οἵτινες ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς ἐγεννήθησαν οὕτως»· οἱ δὲ ὑπὸ ἀνθρωπίνων λόγων προτρεπόμενοι· οἱ δὲ διὰ τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ προθέσει τῆς τῶν οὐρανῶν βασιλείας τὸ ἐπιθυμητικὸν ἐκτεμόντες. Οὐ χρὴ δὲ σωματικῶς ἀκρωτηριάζειν ἑαυτούς· καρπὸς γὰρ τοῦ πνεύματος καὶ ἡ ἐγκράτεια.
orientation: Origen is concluding his long argument that the three kinds of eunuchs in Matthew 19:12 must be read spiritually, not as a command to bodily mutilation.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning the three eunuchisms spiritually. The earlier friends of the letter smoothed the third one bodily to the two; but we, wishing to preserve the sequence of the three eunuchisms and approving the figurative interpretation of the third, will say such things also about the earlier two: eunuchs figuratively would be said to be those inactive toward sexual pleasures. And there are three differences of those inactive toward these things: some are such from constitution, concerning whom: 'There are eunuchs who were born thus from their mother's womb'; others are urged on by human words; others cut out the desiring part for the sake of the word of God by the purpose of the kingdom of heaven. And one must not mutilate oneself bodily; for self-control is also a fruit of the Spirit.

lemmas.gloss: the desiring part, the faculty of desire

choices.why: Keeps the abstract noun parallel to the source, matching the glossary term 'eunuchs' while preserving the -ism formation Origen uses for the three kinds.
The verb means to level or make even; Origen says the literalists made the third kind conform bodily to the first two, flattening the distinction.
Tropos-logia is Origen's technical term for the moral or figurative sense; 'figurative interpretation' is plain and accurate.
Argos means idle or not working; the phrase means those who do not engage in sexual activity, rendered literally without importing later ascetic vocabulary.
Kataskeue means natural formation or makeup; 'from constitution' preserves the sense of an innate condition rather than a choice.
The articular adjective names the desiring faculty of the soul; 'cut out' keeps the surgical metaphor Origen uses for the spiritual act.

bible_refs.note: Εἰσὶν εὐνοῦχοι οἵτινες ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς ἐγεννήθησαν οὕτως
καρπὸς γὰρ τοῦ πνεύματος καὶ ἡ ἐγκράτεια

pass_b_english: On the three eunuchisms, understood spiritually. The earlier friends of the letter smoothed the third kind bodily to match the first two. But we, wanting to preserve the sequence of the three eunuchisms and approving the figurative interpretation of the third, will say the same kind of thing about the first two as well: figuratively, eunuchs are those who are inactive toward sexual pleasures. There are three differences among those who are inactive toward these things. Some are so from constitution, about whom he says, "There are eunuchs who were born that way from their mother's womb" (Matthew 19:12). Others are prompted by human reasoning. Still others, for the sake of the word of God, cut out the desiring part by deliberate intention for the kingdom of heaven. But one must not mutilate oneself bodily, for self-control is also a fruit of the Spirit.

last_rejected.quote: smoothed the third kind bodily to match the first two
last_rejected.source_quote: τὸν τρίτον σωματικῶς τοῖς δυσὶν ἐξωμάλισαν
last_rejected.why: ἐξωμάλισαν means 'leveled' or 'made equal to,' not 'smoothed to match'; the friends of the letter made the third equal to the first two by bodily interpretation.
last_rejected.fix: leveled the third bodily to the first two
last_rejected.ruling: ἐξωμάλισαν means 'made equal/level'; 'smoothed to match' conveys this adequately within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: There are three differences among those who are inactive toward these things
last_rejected.source_quote: Διαφοραὶ δὲ τῶν πρὸς ταῦτα ἀργούντων τρεῖς
last_rejected.why: The Greek says 'three differences of those who are inactive toward these things,' meaning three kinds/types, not that there are three differences among them.
last_rejected.fix: There are three kinds of those who are inactive toward these things
last_rejected.ruling: Διαφοραὶ here means 'differences/kinds'; rendering as 'three differences among' is within normal semantic range.

last_rejected.quote: Others are prompted by human reasoning
last_rejected.source_quote: οἱ δὲ ὑπὸ ἀνθρωπίνων λόγων προτρεπόμενοι
last_rejected.why: λόγων here means 'words' or 'persuasions,' not 'reasoning'; these are persuaded by human words/arguments, not self-prompted by reasoning.
last_rejected.fix: Others are persuaded by human words
last_rejected.ruling: ἀνθρωπίνων λόγων = 'human words/arguments'; 'human reasoning' is within normal range of λόγος meaning.

last_rejected.quote: cut out the desiring part by deliberate intention for the kingdom of heaven
last_rejected.source_quote: διὰ τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ προθέσει τῆς τῶν οὐρανῶν βασιλείας τὸ ἐπιθυμητικὸν ἐκτεμόντες
last_rejected.why: The syntax is misread: 'for the word of God, by deliberate intention of the kingdom of heaven, having cut out the desiring part'—the kingdom is the object of προθέσει, not a purpose 'for' it.
last_rejected.fix: for the word of God, by deliberate choice for the kingdom of heaven, cut out the desiring part
last_rejected.ruling: προθέσει τῆς βασιλείας = 'intention for the kingdom'; genitive with πρόθεσις naturally expresses purpose/goal, not error.
